## ✨ New Features and Changes

Flare 3.0 is here! I know 2.0 came out barely a month ago, so another major version already is a little weird. I've just been super motivated to put some work into Flare, and this update grew into something that deserves 3.0. There's a lot here, from a full role system and stronger sign-in security to archive tools and a much nicer way to move through a large library.

There are real compatibility changes behind the version number too: roles replace the old user/admin model, custom dashboard clients need updated account fields, and everyone will sign in again after upgrading. I've covered those below and in the upgrade guide.

- **Roles and permissions:** create your own roles, assign several to an account, and choose exactly who can upload, share, moderate, manage users, change settings, or configure integrations. Everyone supplies the baseline, with hierarchy and delegation rules for additional roles. Existing administrators keep full access.
- **Two-factor authentication and passkeys:** set up an authenticator app with recovery codes, or sign in with your device or security key. An optional **Require passkey to sign in** setting blocks password and SSO sign-in for your account and provides a separate emergency recovery set. Adding a passkey alone keeps your other sign-in methods available.
- **Sessions and login history:** see where you're signed in, review successful and failed sign-ins, revoke one browser, or sign out everywhere from Profile. API and uploader credentials remain separate.
- **Audit log:** investigate uploads, sharing, deletions, authentication, permissions, settings, integrations, archives, and invites. Search by filename or actor, filter outcomes, and inspect recorded details, even after the original file or account is gone.
- **Archive tools:** browse ZIP, TAR, TAR.GZ/TGZ, and GZIP files, search their paths, preview text and images, and download individual entries. Extract into your library with the folder structure preserved, or package selected files into ZIP or TAR.GZ. Shared archive pages have browsing and entry downloads too. New outputs start private; you can explicitly choose an upload profile instead.
- **A continuous file library:** scroll through your whole library with a date rail for jumping straight to older uploads. Only nearby rows are rendered, selections survive scrolling, and opening a file then going Back restores your place. Desktop, mobile, keyboard navigation, and existing filters all work together.
- **Invite links:** let people create an account while public registration stays closed. Set uses, expiration, and optional roles, revoke links, and see who joined. Invitations start administrator-only; you can enable them for selected roles or everyone.
- **Release-matched docs:** browse dated handbook archives, compare releases, and explicitly open rolling documentation. **Documentation** in Settings and **Setup guide** during setup take you to the guides for your installed version.
- **Storage reliability and fixes:** account deletion now queues recoverable cleanup that survives restarts and retries failures, with recorded upload destinations helping it target the right storage. Avatar cleanup is safer too. Empty S3 thumbnails and moderator previews of private/password-protected images are fixed, alongside account-switch privacy, selected-file metadata, and dependency updates.

The goal I have for Flare going forward is a file vault you can really make yours, configurable right down to the smallest details for whatever use case you have. That might be a personal screenshot host, a family library, or a shared workspace with its own permissions and workflows. I want strong, easy defaults out of the box, with more room to customize as you need it. Appearance, uploads, sharing, access, and automation are all part of that direction.

There's plenty more I want to build, so expect more updates. Keep the suggestions coming, especially the little things that would make Flare fit how you actually use it.

## ⬆️ Updating

Back up your database and uploads first, preserve your existing secrets, and stop old application replicas before upgrading. The Docker image runs migrations automatically. **Everyone will need to sign in again.** Existing accounts, files, links, and uploader credentials remain supported; former administrators receive Admin, and Everyone preserves existing personal capabilities.

- Custom dashboard clients must replace the old `role` field with `roleIds` for writes, `roles` for responses, and `roleId` for filtering. Named tokens keep their scopes and also follow their owner's current permissions.
- Authenticator 2FA and required-passkey sign-in stay off until you enable them. Invitations start administrator-only. Keep `NEXTAUTH_SECRET` unchanged; it protects newly enrolled authenticator secrets.
- Restart unfinished multipart uploads that began before the storage-provenance migration. Historical cleanup jobs with unknown destinations wait for operator verification.
- Audit history starts with this feature and has no automatic retention cutoff. Archive processing has fixed size and format limits; RAR, 7z, and encrypted archives are unsupported.
- Rollback requires the old image and its matching pre-upgrade database and file backup. Changing the image alone cannot undo the role migration.

[Upgrade guide: 2.1 → 3.0](https://flintsh.github.io/Flare/versions/v3.0.0/hosting/maintenance.html#upgrading-from-2-1-to-3-0) · [Full changelog: v2.1.0 → v3.0.0](https://github.com/FlintSH/Flare/compare/v2.1.0...v3.0.0)

## 📦 Download & Deploy

AMD64 and ARM64 images:

```bash
# Docker Hub
docker pull docker.io/flintsh/flare:3.0.0

# GitHub Container Registry
docker pull ghcr.io/flintsh/flare:3.0.0
```
